newsitem.title: ITALY: Dutch to unveil EU treaty draft on March 25 - Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Dutch to unveil EU treaty draft on March 25 - Prodi.

text.p: A new draft of the treaty governing the workings of the European Union will be presented in Rome on March 25 by the Dutch EU presidency, Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Thursday.

"The process of integration will be given a new impetus by the completion of the revision of the Treaty in the context of the intergovernmental conference," (IGC) Prodi told the Senate in a speech before parliamentary question time.
"Thanks also to our commitment, the Dutch presidency will present the new draft of the Treaty on March 25 in Rome."
"The document, which assimilates many of our proposals, will be put to the heads of state and government at the European Council in Amsterdam in June," Prodi added.
Prodi said the aim was to make the European Union "more efficient in its own workings and more democratic in its decision-making processes."
Italy hosts a special meeting of EU foreign ministers in Rome on March 25 to commemorate the 40th anniversary of one of the bloc's founding documents, the Treaty of Rome.

The meeting will also double as an opportunity for ministers to discuss negotiations on drafting a new EU treaty to reform the bloc's institutions ahead of an expected enlargement into eastern Europe.
With the EU planning expansion, the union argues that the systems it set up for six countries 40 years ago are no longer adequate.

The bloc is publicly committed to completing its new treaty by the Amsterdam summit in order to begin enlargement but EU officials privately admit that agreement is likely to be delayed by the British election, expected on May 1.
